title: Hydrogen Peroxide Assisted Soil Sample Digestion for ICP-MS Analysis
author: Sabine Ambrosius

steps.title: Collect and label soil samples
steps.instruction: Collect representative soil from the experimental site, mix samples from several locations, consider sampling depth, and keep samples in clean containers.

steps.title: Remove debris and dry soil
steps.instruction: Mix the collected soil, remove stones, wood, plant material, then dry in an oven at 40 °C–60 °C until weight is constant; drying can be done in 50 mL conical tubes or trays.

steps.title: Reduce particle size
steps.instruction: Hand‑mill large pieces with a metal‑free mortar and pestle or crush by hand; optionally sieve using a non‑metal sieve while avoiding metal contamination.

steps.title: Weigh soil aliquot
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 100 mg of the dried soil into the first set of metal‑free 15 mL conical centrifuge tubes and record the exact weight; if more than 100 mg is needed, use 50 mL tubes.

steps.title: Label digestion and storage tubes
steps.instruction: Label two sets of metal‑free 15 mL conical centrifuge tubes – the first set for digestion and the second set for the final diluted samples; larger (50 mL) tubes may be used when needed.

steps.title: Add first acid aliquot
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of 30 % HNO₃ to each tube and incubate at room temperature for at least 2 hours; slurry formation is normal.

steps.title: Add second acid and overnight digestion
steps.instruction: Add another 500 µL of 30 % HNO₃ (total 1 mL per tube), loosely tighten the screw caps, and place the tubes in a water bath at 65 °C overnight.

steps.title: Check slurry separation
steps.instruction: The next day, verify that each sample has separated into a liquid phase and solid phase; if not, increase the volume of 30 % HNO₃ (and proportionally H₂O₂ and water in later steps) and repeat the overnight incubation.

steps.title: High‑temperature boil
steps.instruction: Raise the water bath temperature to 95 °C and boil the samples for at least 30 minutes; avoid boil‑over and be cautious of acid fumes when opening the tubes.

steps.title: Cool before peroxide
steps.instruction: Remove the tubes from the water bath and allow them to cool completely to room temperature before adding hydrogen peroxide.

steps.title: Add hydrogen peroxide
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 30 % H₂O₂ (or 300 µL if the total HNO₃ added was 1.5 mL) and return the tubes to the 95 °C water bath for 30 minutes; handle the foaming reaction carefully.

steps.title: Dilute with ultrapure water
steps.instruction: After cooling, slowly add 8.8 mL of Type I ultrapure water (resistivity 18.2 MΩ·cm at 25 °C), invert the tubes to mix; increase the water volume proportionally if more acid was used, and use a larger tube if the total volume exceeds the tube capacity.

steps.title: Overnight cold storage
steps.instruction: Store the tubes at 4 °C overnight (longer storage is possible).

steps.title: Centrifuge digests
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 12 000 × g, 4 °C for 2 hours; ensure the tubes can withstand the force, otherwise reduce g and increase time; if a refrigerated centrifuge is unavailable, keep samples at 4 °C before centrifugation; repeat centrifugation or filter if particles remain unsettled.

steps.title: Prepare diluted samples
steps.instruction: In each tube of the second set, add 3.2 mL of 2 % HNO₃, then add 800 µL of the supernatant to achieve a 1:5 dilution.

steps.title: Store diluted samples
steps.instruction: Store the diluted samples at 4 °C until ICP‑MS analysis; note that prolonged storage may affect stability of some elements.

steps.title: Final precipitation check
steps.instruction: Immediately before ICP‑MS, inspect each sample for precipitate; if present, centrifuge again at 4 °C for at least 30 minutes and transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Calculate dilution factors
steps.instruction: Compute the preliminary dilution factor: pre‑DF = (final reaction volume [mL] × 1000) / sample weight [mg]. Then calculate the final dilution factor: DF = pre‑DF × 5. Record these values for data correction.
